title: ハナミズキ (Hanamizuki — Flowering Dogwood)
description:
One of the most beloved Japanese pop songs of the 21st century. Written and performed by 一青窈 (Hitoto Yō), released on February 11, 2004, with music by マシコタツロウ (Mashiko Tatsurō) and arrangement by 武部聡志 (Takebe Satoshi). The song was written in the months after the September 11, 2001 attacks as a quiet prayer for peace — the dogwood (ハナミズキ) is a tree that was gifted by the US to Japan and by Japan to the US as symbols of friendship.

The lyric imagines being on a sinking ship with the person you love: instead of hoping to be saved together, the narrator wishes for the beloved and *that person's* beloved to be happy for a hundred years — a selfless, quietly devastating statement. The song spent a record-breaking 125 consecutive weeks on the Oricon weekly singles chart and remains one of Japan's most-performed karaoke songs.

For learners: Excellent N3 material in a slow ballad tempo ideal for reading along. 一青窈's diction is very clear. Key vocabulary: 空を押し上げて (pushing up the sky), 水際 (water's edge / shoreline), つぼみ (bud / blossom not yet opened), 薄紅色 (pale crimson / blush pink), 果てない夢 (endless dream), 果てない波 (endless waves), 我慢 (patience / endurance), 実を結ぶ (to bear fruit / come to fruition), ひらり (lightly / flutteringly), 白い帆 (white sail), 母の日 (Mother's Day). The grammar is poetic but not archaic; intermediate learners will encounter real literary Japanese without feeling buried.
